literal: At first limited: counties with households not filling one hundred were abolished.
idiomatic: At first he abolished any county with fewer than a hundred households.

literal: Summer, fourth month: ordered Secretariat Gentleman Gongsun Biao as envoy to the lands south of the Yangtze, to observe Huan Xuan's signs of rebellion.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer he sent Gongsun Biao of the Secretariat to the south to watch Huan Xuan.

literal: Encountered Xuan's defeat and returned.
idiomatic: He arrived as Xuan fell and returned.

literal: Rouran Shelun's younger cousin Yue attacked Dana and others, plotting to kill Shelun and establish Dana.
idiomatic: Yue, Shelun's cousin among the Rouran, plotted with Dana and others to kill Shelun and set Dana up in his place.

literal: The plot was discovered; they came fleeing in submission.
idiomatic: The plot was discovered and they fled to submit.

literal: Fifth month: established smelteries east of the mountains, mobilized convicts and exiles from provinces and commanderies to forge arms and armor.
idiomatic: In the fifth month he set up smelteries in the east and drafted convicts from the provinces to forge arms.

literal: Autumn, ninth month: the emperor attended Zhaoyang Hall, separately set the host of offices, summoned civil and military court ministers, personally selected them, measured ability and appointed use.
idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn he held court at Zhaoyang Hall, reorganized the bureaucracy, and personally chose men for office according to their talents.

literal: Established four noble ranks, saying "king, duke, marquis, viscount," abolishing the titles of earl and baron.
idiomatic: He fixed four noble ranks — king, duke, marquis, and viscount — and abolished the ranks of earl and baron.

literal: Posthumously recorded old ministers, adding enfeoffments and ranks, each according to merit.
idiomatic: He posthumously honored old ministers with titles and ranks according to merit.

literal: That autumn, great disorder in the lands south of the Yangtze; floating migrants swaddled on back fled to north of the Huai; on the road one followed another.
idiomatic: That autumn the south fell into chaos, and refugees swarmed north across the Huai in an unbroken stream.

literal: Winter, tenth month, day xinsi: great amnesty, changed the era name.
idiomatic: On the xinsi day of the tenth month of winter he proclaimed a general amnesty and a new reign title.

literal: Built the Western Palace.
idiomatic: He built the Western Palace.

literal: Eleventh month: the emperor visited the Western Palace, great selection of court ministers, ordered each to distinguish his clan lineage, guarantee and recommend talent and conduct; sons and grandsons of various divisions who had lost livelihood were granted ranks, more than two thousand persons.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month he went to the Western Palace, ordered the court to sort clans and recommend talent, and ennobled more than two thousand men of the tribal nobility who had fallen on hard times.

literal: Twelfth month, day wuchen: the imperial carriage visited Chai Mountain Palace.
idiomatic: On the wuchen day of the twelfth month the court visited Chai Mountain Palace.

literal: That year, the island barbarian Liu Yu raised troops and executed Huan Xuan.
idiomatic: That year Liu Yu of the eastern isles rose and killed Huan Xuan.

literal: Year 2, spring, second month, day guihai: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: In the second year, on the guihai day of the second month of spring, the court returned to the palace.

literal: Summer, fourth month: the imperial carriage performed the ceremony at the western suburb; carriage banners all black.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer he sacrificed at the western suburb with all banners black.

literal: That year, Sima Dezong again presumptuously established himself.
idiomatic: That year Sima Dezong again took the throne.

literal: Murong De died; elder brother's son Chao presumptuously established himself.
idiomatic: Murong De died and his nephew Chao seized power.

literal: Year 3, spring, first month, day jiashen: the imperial carriage northern tour, visited Chai Mountain Palace.
idiomatic: In the third year, on the jiashen day of the first month of spring, the court toured north to Chai Mountain Palace.

literal: Conducted a hunt, reaching Wugu Mountain.
idiomatic: He hunted as far as Wugu Mountain.

literal: Second month, day yihai: visited Dai Garden Mountain, built the Five Stone Pavilion.
idiomatic: On the yihai day of the second month he went to Dai Garden Mountain and built the Five Stone Pavilion.

literal: Third month, day gengzi: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: On the gengzi day of the third month he returned to the palace.

literal: Summer, fourth month, day gengshen: again visited Chai Mountain Palace.
idiomatic: On the gengshen day of the fourth month of summer he again went to Chai Mountain Palace.

literal: Bestowed appointment on Editorial Director Wang Yidi to make the military classic Guxu Licheng Diagram of three hundred sixty seasons.
idiomatic: He appointed the editorial director Wang Yidi to compile a three-hundred-and-sixty-part treatise on military formations.

literal: Thereupon ascended Dingxiang Jiaoshi Mountain, again visited Macheng.
idiomatic: He then climbed Jiaoshi Mountain in Dingxiang and went on to Macheng.

literal: On day jiawu, the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: On the jiawu day he returned to the palace.

literal: That month, the Rouran raided the frontier; at night troops were summoned; at dawn the bandits fled; then stopped.
idiomatic: That month the Rouran raided the border; troops were called up by night, but the enemy fled by dawn and the alarm was stood down.

literal: Sixth month: mobilized men from the eight divisions within five hundred li to build the Leinan Palace; gate towers more than ten zhang high.
idiomatic: In the sixth month he drafted men from the eight divisions within five hundred li to build the Leinan Palace, with gate towers more than ten zhang high.

literal: Led canals and dug pools, broadened parks and preserves.
idiomatic: Canals were dug and the parks enlarged.

literal: Planned to establish an outer city, twenty li square, separately set wards and markets, main roads penetrating through.
idiomatic: He planned an outer city twenty li square, with wards, markets, and thoroughfares.

literal: Thirty days and stopped.
idiomatic: The work was halted after thirty days.

literal: Autumn, seventh month: Grand Marshal Mu Chong died.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Mu Chong died.

literal: Eighth month, day jiachen: traveled to Chai Mountain Palace, then reached Blue Ox Mountain.
idiomatic: On the jiachen day of the eighth month he went to Chai Mountain Palace and on to Blue Ox Mountain.

literal: On day bingchen, west ascended Wuyao North Plain, viewed the ninety-nine springs, built a stone pavilion, then went to the stone desert.
idiomatic: On the bingchen day he climbed the Wuyao north plain, viewed the ninety-nine springs, built a stone pavilion, and entered the stone desert.

literal: Ninth month, day jiaxu on the new moon: visited the salt pool south of the desert.
idiomatic: On the new moon of the ninth month, the jiaxu day, he visited the salt pool south of the desert.

literal: On day renwu, reached the center of the desert, viewed the heavenly salt pool.
idiomatic: On the renwu day he reached the heart of the desert and viewed the heavenly salt pool.

literal: Crossed the desert, north to the Tu salt pool.
idiomatic: He crossed the desert north to the Tu salt pool.

literal: On day guisi, returned south to Changchuan.
idiomatic: On the guisi day he turned south to Changchuan.

literal: On day bingshen, overlooked Chang Marsh.
idiomatic: On the bingshen day he overlooked Chang Marsh.

literal: Winter, tenth month, day gengshen: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: On the gengshen day of the tenth month of winter he returned to the palace.

literal: Year 4, spring, second month: enfeoffed the imperial son Xiu as Prince of Hejian, Chuwen as Prince of Changle, Lian as Prince of Guangping, Li as Prince of Jingzhao.
idiomatic: In the fourth year, in the second month of spring, he enfeoffed Xiu as prince of Hejian, Chuwen as prince of Changle, Lian as prince of Guangping, and Li as prince of Jingzhao.

literal: Summer, fifth month: northern tour.
idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer he toured the north.

literal: From Canhe Marsh east past Panyang Mountain, great rain, sudden water carried off several hundred baggage wagons, killed more than a hundred persons.
idiomatic: East from Canhe Marsh past Panyang Mountain a cloudburst swept away hundreds of wagons and killed more than a hundred men.

literal: Thereupon northeast crossed the stone desert, reached Changchuan, visited Ruyuan.
idiomatic: He crossed the stone desert northeast to Changchuan and went on to Ruyuan.

literal: Prince of Changshan Zun had crime and was granted death.
idiomatic: Prince Zun of Changshan was found guilty and ordered to take his own life.

literal: Autumn, seventh month: the imperial carriage from Ruyuan west visited Canhe Marsh.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn he went west from Ruyuan to Canhe Marsh.

literal: Built the north palace wall; thirty days and stopped; then returned to the palace.
idiomatic: He built the north palace wall in thirty days, then returned to the capital.

literal: Eighth month: visited Chai Mountain Palace.
idiomatic: In the eighth month he went to Chai Mountain Palace.

literal: That month, executed Minister of Works Yu Yue.
idiomatic: That month he executed Yu Yue, minister of works.

literal: Winter, eleventh month: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter he returned to the palace.

literal: That year, Murong Bao's adopted son Gao Yun killed Xi and established himself; Helian Qu Fu styled himself Great Chanyu, Great King of Summer.
idiomatic: That year Gao Yun, Bao's adopted son, killed Xi and seized the throne; Helian Qu Fu declared himself Great Chanyu and Great King of Summer.

literal: Year 5, spring, first month: traveled to Chai Mountain Palace, then to Canhe Marsh, viewed fishing on the Yan River, [13] reaching Ningchuan.
idiomatic: In the fifth year, in the first month of spring, he went to Chai Mountain Palace and Canhe Marsh, fished on the Yan River, [13] and reached Ningchuan.

literal: Third month: Yao Xing sent envoys with court tribute.
idiomatic: In the third month Yao Xing sent envoys to court.

literal: That year, the imperial grandson Tao was born.
idiomatic: That year the imperial grandson Tao was born.

literal: Year 6, summer: the emperor was unwell.
idiomatic: In the sixth year, in summer, the emperor fell ill.

literal: Earlier, the emperor took cold-food powder; from after Medical Director Yin Qiang died, the medicine several times stirred outbreaks, reaching here ever more severe.
idiomatic: He had long taken cold-food powder; after the medical director Yin Qiang died the doses brought on ever fiercer attacks.

literal: Yet calamities and anomalies repeatedly appeared; worried and vexed, ill at ease; sometimes several days without eating, sometimes not sleeping until dawn.
idiomatic: Omens multiplied, his mind grew troubled, and he would go days without food or sleep until dawn.

literal: He blamed the host below; joy and anger contrary to constant; said the hundred officials and attendants left and right were not to be trusted; feared as in the astronomical prognostication, there might be trouble at the elbow and armpit.
idiomatic: He turned on his ministers, raged without cause, and trusted no one around him, fearing the court prognostications of treason at his side.

literal: Recalling past success and failure, gain and loss, all day and night alone he spoke without stopping, as if ghostly things beside him answered and responded.
idiomatic: He brooded over past victories and defeats, talking to himself day and night as though ghosts answered back.

literal: Court ministers who came before him — he pursued their old wrongs and all were killed; the rest, whether facial color changed, or breath not regulated, or gait not in measure, or speech and deportment in error — the emperor all considered that malice was in the heart and change appeared outside; then personally beat and struck them; the dead were all displayed before Tian'an Hall.
idiomatic: Ministers who came before him were killed for old grudges, or for a changed expression, uneven breathing, awkward step, or a slip of the tongue. He beat them to death himself and had the bodies displayed before Tian'an Hall.

literal: Thereupon court and countryside, people's feelings each harbored peril and fear; responsible offices were slack, none mutually supervised and urged; the hundred crafts stole and plundered; bandits and thieves walked openly; between lanes and alleys people were few.
idiomatic: Court and country lived in terror. Officials neglected their duties, craftsmen looted, and thieves walked openly until the streets were nearly empty.

literal: The emperor also heard of it and said: "I let it become so; wait until the disaster year passes, and I shall again clear and govern it.
idiomatic: When he heard of it he said, "I brought this on myself. After the bad year passes I will set things right again."

literal: Autumn, seventh month: Murong branch families more than a hundred households plotted to flee outward; discovered; executed in secret; dead numbered more than three hundred.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn more than a hundred Murong households plotted to flee; the plot was discovered and more than three hundred were executed.

literal: Eighth month: Prince of Wei Yi plotted rebellion, granted death.
idiomatic: In the eighth month Prince Yi of Wei plotted treason and was ordered to die.

literal: Winter, tenth month, day wuchen: the emperor died at Tian'an Hall; at the time age thirty-nine.
idiomatic: On the wuchen day of the tenth month of winter he died in Tian'an Hall at the age of thirty-nine.

literal: Yongxing year 2, ninth month, day jiayin: posthumous title Emperor Xuanwu, buried at Shengle Jinling, temple name Taizu.
idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxing, on the jiayin day of the ninth month, he was given the posthumous title Emperor Xuanwu, buried at Jinling in Shengle, with temple name Taizu.

literal: [14] Taichang year 5, changed posthumous title to Daowu.
idiomatic: [14] In the fifth year of Taichang his posthumous title was changed to Daowu.

literal: The historian says: The house of Jin collapsed and parted; Rong and Jie rode the opportunity; presumptuous and false tangled in confusion; jackals and wolves competed in the chase.
idiomatic: The historian writes: When the house of Jin fell apart, the barbarians seized their chance; pretenders multiplied and wolves competed for the prey.

literal: Taizu, within showing and hiding, safety and peril, bending and stretching, lurking and leaping, drove and led the remnant masses, roused their spirit and martial power, was able to cut down regional difficulties, then opened the central land, court bowed to man and spirit, clearly ascended the imperial pole.
idiomatic: Taizu, through danger and concealment, roused the remnant peoples, swept away his rivals, opened the central plains, and took the throne in truth.

literal: Though cap and shoes had no leisure, he dwelled in haste on outer soil, yet institutions, standards, and plans all endured for long generations.
idiomatic: Though he wandered long in exile, the institutions he founded endured for generations.

literal: What is called the great man's favorable seeing, the hundred people sharing in his power — perhaps suppressing unworldly spirit and martialness.
idiomatic: Truly he was the great man of the Changes, the ruler the people could follow — a martial spirit not of this world.

literal: Yet hardship and obstruction had their term; calamity arose beyond calculation — will it be that human affairs were insufficient, or did Heaven truly do it?
idiomatic: Yet his term was cut short and disaster came unlooked for — was it only human failure, or did Heaven itself decree it?

literal: Alas!
idiomatic: Alas!

literal: Collation notes
idiomatic: Collation notes

literal: Winter, tenth month of year 7: all editions read "year 2" for "year 7."
idiomatic: On "winter, tenth month of year 7": all editions read "year 2" instead of "year 7."

literal: Northern History volume 1 Wei Basic Annals 1, Cefu volume 6
idiomatic: Northern History 1, Wei Annals 1; Cefu 6

literal: 〈page 64〉
Has "year 7."
idiomatic: read "year 7."

literal: According to Fu Jian's defeat at Fei River in Jin Taiyuan year 8
idiomatic: Fu Jian's defeat at the Fei River fell in Jin Taiyuan year 8

literal: , Tuoba Gui's so-called year 2 before establishing era names was year 378, clearly an error; now corrected according to the above.
idiomatic: (383); Tuoba Gui's pre-reign "year 2" would be 378, which is clearly wrong — corrected accordingly.

literal: Liu Xian's younger brother Feini led cavalry to plunder the Nuzhen tribe: in Northern, Ji, Dian, and Ju four editions "Feini" all read "Kangni"; Baibaina and Nan editions read "Feini."
idiomatic: On "Liu Xian's brother Feini": the Northern, Ji, Dian, and Ju editions read "Kangni"; the Baibaina and Nan editions read "Feini."

literal: According to the text below and Biography of Liu Xian in volume 23, both call Xian's younger brother "Kangni" or "Kanglei"; one does not hear of another younger brother named "Feini."
idiomatic: Below and in Liu Xian's biography (j. 23) the brother is called Kangni or Kanglei, not Feini.

literal: It seems "Kangni" is correct.
idiomatic: Kangni therefore seems correct.

literal: But Cefu volume 6
idiomatic: But Cefu 6

literal: 〈page 64〉
, Zizhi Tongjian volume 106
idiomatic: and Zizhi Tongjian 106

literal: 〈page 3367〉
at this place both read "Feini."
idiomatic: both read Feini here.

literal: Moreover here it first says Feini came to submit, next month again says Liu Xian sent his younger brother Kangni to welcome Kudou — then he also had not yet submitted to Tuoba Gui, or there was another person; now follow Baibaina edition.
idiomatic: Yet here Feini submits, while the next month Xian sends Kangni to welcome Kudou — so he had not yet submitted to Tuoba Gui, or another man is meant. The Baibaina text is followed here.

literal: At the emperor's left and right, Yu Huan and others: in Northern, Ji, Dian, and Ju four editions "Huan" reads "Zhi."
idiomatic: On "Yu Huan at the emperor's side": the Northern, Ji, Dian, and Ju editions read Zhi for Huan.

literal: Baibaina and Nan editions read "Huan."
idiomatic: The Baibaina and Nan editions read Huan.

literal: According to Northern History volume 1, Zizhi Tongjian volume 106
idiomatic: Northern History 1 and Zizhi Tongjian 106

literal: 〈page 3368〉
also read "Huan."
idiomatic: also read Huan.

literal: Now follow Baibaina edition.
idiomatic: The Baibaina reading is adopted.

literal: See collation note to juan 27.
idiomatic: See the collation note to juan 27.

literal: Kumo division chief Jiuji left behind the scattered: Northern History volume 1 has the character Xi after "Kumo."
idiomatic: On "Kumo chief Jiuji": Northern History 1 inserts Xi after Kumo.

literal: According to Kumo Xi, or simply called "Xi," one should not simply call "Kumo" — here the character Xi is probably missing.
idiomatic: The tribe is Kumo Xi, or simply Xi — not Kumo alone; Xi has probably dropped out here.
